searchDocs.title: Localize library methods​
searchDocs.content: By localizing library methods, you avoid table lookup every time you need to call the function  local Serialize = Dynamo.Serialize for i = 1, 1e5 do -- ... Serialize(...) -- avoid table lookups in hot paths end

searchDocs.title: Prefer Serialize1 / Deserialize1 for single values​
searchDocs.content: Variadic Serialize / Deserialize are ideal for multi-value packets. For one value, the *1 APIs avoid packing/unpacking overhead and return the next offset when you need framing.

searchDocs.title: Account for type tags in size budgets​
searchDocs.content: Every value costs +1 byte for its tag, including nested array elements and map keys/values. Schemaless flexibility trades some bandwidth versus a fixed schema with known field types.

searchDocs.title: Instance references vs value schemas​
searchDocs.content: References (RefInstance, default): same instance identity across the network when _VSID is replicated. Use SetConstant("InstanceRefMode", "Extended") if you need more than 65,535 live ids.SerInstance: property snapshot into a new instance; requires DefineSerInstanceSchema and SetConstant("SerInstanceSerialization", true).  Do not mix expectations: a reference does not recreate missing instances, and SerInstance does not preserve the original Instance object. Both peers must agree on these constants.

searchDocs.title: CFrame size vs precision​
searchDocs.content: With quaternion mode enabled (default via UseQuaternion), CFrames use 28 payload bytes plus a tag. Matrix mode (SetConstant("UseQuaternion", false)) uses 48 payload bytes. Quaternion reconstruction is lossy relative to a full matrix; measure against your accuracy needs.

searchDocs.title: UDim scale quantization​
searchDocs.content: UDim / UDim2 scales are quantized to 16 bits over QuantizedScaleMin…QuantizedScaleMax (default 0…1). Offsets use i16. Widen the range with SetConstant if you need scales outside 0…1, and test GUI values that matter if you need exact floats.

searchDocs.title: Basic workflow​
searchDocs.content: Serialize one or more values into a buffer.Send or store that buffer.Deserialize the buffer back into values.  local Dynamo = require(path.to.Dynamo) local encoded = Dynamo.Serialize1({ Health = 100, Name = "Builder", Position = Vector3.new(4, 8, 15), }) local decoded = Dynamo.Deserialize1(encoded) print(decoded.Name, decoded.Health, decoded.Position)   Unlike schema-driven libraries, the buffer is self-describing at the type level: each value begins with a type tag, then its payload. Nested tables, arrays, and maps carry tags for every element and key.

searchDocs.title: What Dynamo is for​
searchDocs.content: Dynamic payloads where a fixed schema would be awkward.Mixed-type packets (Serialize / Deserialize accept multiple values).Game datatypes such as Vector3, CFrame, Color3, UDim2, Enum, and Instance references.  Continue with Installation, then the API and Type catalog. Measured throughput and comparisons are in Benchmarks.

searchDocs.title: Wally​
searchDocs.content: Add Dynamo to your wally.toml dependencies:  Dynamo = "elentium/dynamo@1.1.0"   Install dependencies:  wally install   Require the generated package from the location mapped by your Rojo project:  local Packages = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Packages local Dynamo = require(Packages.Dynamo)

searchDocs.title: Pesde​
searchDocs.content: pesde add elentium/dynamo   Require the package through the path generated by your Pesde setup:  local Dynamo = require(path.to.Dynamo)

searchDocs.title: npm​
searchDocs.content: npm install @elentium/dynamo   Use your npm package import path as usual.  For roblox-ts, add @elentium to your project's typeRoots and mapnode_modules/@elentium in your Rojo project tree.

searchDocs.title: Source​
searchDocs.content: You can also copy src/Dynamo.luau from this repository into your project and require it directly.

searchDocs.title: Numbers​
searchDocs.content: Tag	When inferred	PayloadU8 / I8	integer in unsigned/signed 8-bit range	1 U16 / I16	integer in 16-bit range	2 U24 / I24	integer in 24-bit range	3 U32 / I32	integer in 32-bit range	4 U40 / I40	integer in 40-bit range	5 U48 / I48	integer in 48-bit range	6 F32	non-integer within F32 magnitude	4 F64	other numbers (including oversized integers)	8  Signed ranges use two’s-complement style bounds (for example I8 from -128). Unsigned ranges are non-negative up to 2^n - 1.

searchDocs.title: Booleans, nil, empty table​
searchDocs.content: Tag	PayloadBool	1 (0 or 1) Nil	0 Void	0 (empty table {})

searchDocs.title: Strings​
searchDocs.content: Tag	Length prefix	Max lengthStr8	u8	255 Str	u16	65,535 Str24	u24	16,777,215  Lengths are bytes, not UTF-8 characters. Payload is the raw string bytes.

searchDocs.title: Buffers​
searchDocs.content: Tag	Length prefix	Max lengthBuf8	u8	255 Buf	u16	65,535 Buf24	u24	16,777,215  Payload is a raw byte copy of the buffer.

searchDocs.title: Arrays and maps​
searchDocs.content: Tables with a non-zero array length (#t ~= 0) & no hash elements serialize as arrays. Otherwise non-empty tables serialize as maps (when map-length compute is enabled, length picks Map8 / Map / Map24).  Tag	Count prefix	Max entriesArray8 / Map8	u8	255 Array / Map	u16	65,535 Array24 / Map24	u24	16,777,215  Each array element is a full tagged value. Each map entry is a tagged key followed by a tagged value.

searchDocs.title: Vectors and Color3​
searchDocs.content: Tag	PayloadVec (Vector3)	3 × f32 (12) Vec2 (Vector2)	2 × f32 (8) Color (Color3)	RGB as 3 × u8 (3)

searchDocs.title: CFrame​
searchDocs.content: Controlled by Dynamo.SetConstant("UseQuaternion", …) (default true):  Tag	PayloadQCframe	position + quaternion, 7 × f32 (28) Cframe	position + 3×3 matrix, 12 × f32 (48)

searchDocs.title: UDim / UDim2​
searchDocs.content: Tag	PayloadUdim	quantized scale u16 + offset i16 (4) Udim2	two UDim payloads (8)  Scale is quantized into [QuantizedScaleMin, QuantizedScaleMax] (default 0…1) across 0…65535. Change the range with SetConstant("QuantizedScaleMin" | "QuantizedScaleMax", …).

searchDocs.title: Enums​
searchDocs.content: Tag	PayloadEnumType (Enum)	u16 enum id EnumItem	u16 parent enum id + u16 item value  Enum ids are assigned from Enum:GetEnums() at module init.

searchDocs.title: Instances​
searchDocs.content: Tag	PayloadRefInstance	u16 id (Normal) or u24 id (Extended) SerInstance	schema id u8, then each property as an untagged payload (schema supplies the type)  Default instance path is reference serialization (Inst → RefInstance when SerInstanceSerialization is false). Switch with:  Dynamo.SetConstant("SerInstanceSerialization", true) -- value schemas Dynamo.SetConstant("InstanceRefMode", "Extended") -- u24 refs   References use the _VSID attribute and in-memory maps:  Server assigns ids to descendants and can reuse ids when instances are removed.Client mirrors replicated _VSID attributes into local maps.  DefineSerInstanceSchema registers value-style schemas for SerInstance (creates a new instance on deserialize).

searchDocs.title: Type tag constants​
searchDocs.content: All public tags are on Dynamo.Types (U8, Str8, Array, Vec, QCframe, RefInstance, SerInstance, …). Tags are stable within a Dynamo version; do not hard-code numeric ids across major versions without checking the module.

searchDocs.title: Serialize​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Serialize( ...: any-- Values to serialize, in order. ) → buffer Serializes one or more values into a new exactly sized buffer. Each value is prefixed with a type tag.

searchDocs.title: SerializeWOffset​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.SerializeWOffset( Offset: number,-- Byte offset where the payload begins. ...: any-- Values to serialize, in order. ) → buffer Serializes values into a new buffer after a zero-filled prefix. Writing starts at Offset. The returned buffer length equals the final cursor (including the reserved prefix). Fill the leading bytes yourself.

searchDocs.title: Serialize1​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Serialize1( Value: any-- Value to serialize. ) → buffer Serializes a single value into a new exactly sized buffer.

searchDocs.title: Serialize1WOffset​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Serialize1WOffset( Value: any,-- Value to serialize. Offset: number-- Byte offset where the payload begins. ) → buffer Serializes a single value after a zero-filled prefix.

searchDocs.title: Deserialize​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Deserialize( Buf: buffer-- Buffer containing encoded values. ) → ...any Deserializes every top-level value from the start of a buffer to its end.

searchDocs.title: DeserializeRange​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.DeserializeRange( Buf: buffer,-- Buffer containing encoded values. Start: number,-- Byte offset at which reading begins. End: number?-- Exclusive end offset. Defaults to buffer length. ) → ...any Deserializes top-level values while the cursor is in [Start, End). End defaults to buffer.len(Buf).

searchDocs.title: Deserialize1​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Deserialize1( Buf: buffer-- Buffer containing an encoded value. ) → ( any,-- Decoded value. number-- Cursor after the value (next unread offset). ) Deserializes a single top-level value from the start of a buffer.

searchDocs.title: Deserialize1WOffset​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Deserialize1WOffset( Buf: buffer,-- Buffer containing an encoded value. Offset: number-- Byte offset at which reading begins. ) → ( any,-- Decoded value. number-- Cursor after the value (next unread offset). ) Deserializes a single top-level value beginning at a byte offset.

searchDocs.title: Push​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Push( Buf: buffer,-- Destination buffer (must already be large enough). Offset: number,-- Byte offset at which writing begins. ...: any-- Values to serialize, in order. ) → number-- Cursor after the write. Writes one or more values into an existing buffer and returns the new cursor. If a push errors mid-write, call Restore so the internal scratch buffer is reset.

searchDocs.title: Push1​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Push1( Buf: buffer,-- Destination buffer (must already be large enough). Offset: number,-- Byte offset at which writing begins. Value: any-- Value to serialize. ) → number-- Cursor after the write. Writes a single value into an existing buffer and returns the new cursor. If a push errors mid-write, call Restore so the internal scratch buffer is reset.

searchDocs.title: Restore​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.Restore() → () Restores the internal write scratch buffer after a failed Push / Push1.

searchDocs.title: SetWriteBufferSize​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.SetWriteBufferSize( Size: number-- New scratch-buffer size in bytes. ) → () Replaces the reusable serialization scratch buffer with a new capacity. The default capacity is 1,000,000 bytes. Existing content up to the previous size is copied when possible.

searchDocs.title: DefineSerInstanceSchema​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.DefineSerInstanceSchema( ClassName: string,-- Instance ClassName this schema applies to. Schema: {[string]: number}-- Property name → type tag id map. ) → () Registers a property schema for value-style instance serialization (SerInstance). Schema values are type-tag ids from Dynamo.Types (for example Dynamo.Types.Vec). Property payloads are untagged (the schema already names the type). Up to 255 schemas may be registered.

searchDocs.title: SetConstant​
searchDocs.content: Core </> Dynamo.SetConstant( Constant: Constants,-- Constant name. Value: any-- New value (boolean, string, or number as required). ) → () Replaces a runtime configuration constant that affects inference / wire layout. Valid names: SerInstanceSerialization, DoMapCompute, InstanceRefMode, UseQuaternion, QuantizedScaleMin, QuantizedScaleMax. Changing SerInstanceSerialization or UseQuaternion updates which type tag Instances / CFrames use on subsequent serialize calls.

searchDocs.title: Round trip a table​
searchDocs.content: local Dynamo = require(path.to.Dynamo) local original = { Coins = 12_500, DisplayName = "Elentium", EquippedItem = 17, } local bytes = Dynamo.Serialize1(original) local restored = Dynamo.Deserialize1(bytes) print(restored.DisplayName, restored.Coins, restored.EquippedItem)

searchDocs.title: Multiple values in one buffer​
searchDocs.content: local packet = Dynamo.Serialize( player.UserId, character:GetPivot(), { 4, 9, 23, 71 } ) local userId, pivot, inventory = Dynamo.Deserialize(packet)

searchDocs.title: Compact inventory array​
searchDocs.content: local itemIds = { 4, 9, 23, 71 } local bytes = Dynamo.Serialize1(itemIds) local restored = Dynamo.Deserialize1(bytes)   With four small integers, Dynamo picks Array8 and U8 elements. Each element still carries a type tag.

searchDocs.title: RemoteEvent payload​
searchDocs.content: -- server local bytes = Dynamo.Serialize1({ Amount = 25, Critical = false, Origin = Vector3.new(10, 2, -4), Target = targetPart, }) DamageEvent:FireClient(player, bytes)   -- client DamageEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(bytes: buffer) local message = Dynamo.Deserialize1(bytes) print(message.Target, message.Amount, message.Critical) end)   Target serializes as an Instance reference when both sides share _VSID maps for that instance.

searchDocs.title: Serializable instance by value​
searchDocs.content: local Dynamo = require(path.to.Dynamo) local T = Dynamo.Types Dynamo.DefineSerInstanceSchema("Part", { Anchored = T.Bool, Color = T.Color, Name = T.Str8, Position = T.Vec, Size = T.Vec, }) Dynamo.SetConstant("SerInstanceSerialization", true) local bytes = Dynamo.Serialize1(somePart) local clone = Dynamo.Deserialize1(bytes) -- new Part with schema properties   When SerInstanceSerialization is true, matching Parts serialize listed properties and deserialize into a new Part. Parent is not included unless you add it yourself after deserialize. Leave the constant false (default) for _VSID instance references instead.

searchDocs.title: Switch CFrame / ref layout​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.SetConstant("UseQuaternion", false) -- matrix CFrame (larger, less lossy) Dynamo.SetConstant("InstanceRefMode", "Extended") -- u24 instance ids   Keep constants in sync on every peer that shares buffers.

searchDocs.title: Preserve an application header​
searchDocs.content: local bytes = Dynamo.Serialize1WOffset({ Id = 7, Message = "ready", }, 2) buffer.writeu8(bytes, 0, 1) buffer.writeu8(bytes, 1, 9) local payload = Dynamo.Deserialize1WOffset(bytes, 2)

searchDocs.title: Push into a preallocated buffer​
searchDocs.content: local out = buffer.create(256) local nextOffset = Dynamo.Push1(out, 0, { Kind = "ping", At = os.clock(), })   Push1 returns the cursor after the written value.

searchDocs.title: Serialize​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.Serialize(...: any) -> buffer Dynamo.Serialize1(Value: any) -> buffer   Writes one or more values into a new buffer. Each value is prefixed with a type tag.  local packet = Dynamo.Serialize(player.UserId, character.HumanoidRootPart.CFrame) local one = Dynamo.Serialize1("ready")

searchDocs.title: Serialize with offset​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.SerializeWOffset(Offset: number, ...: any) -> buffer Dynamo.Serialize1WOffset(Value: any, Offset: number) -> buffer   Same as serialize, but writing starts at Offset. The returned buffer has length equal to the final cursor (so it includes leading bytes reserved for a header). Leading bytes before Offset are zero-filled until you write them.  local bytes = Dynamo.Serialize1WOffset(payload, 2) buffer.writeu8(bytes, 0, 1) -- version buffer.writeu8(bytes, 1, 9) -- opcode

searchDocs.title: Deserialize​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.Deserialize(Buf: buffer) -> ...any Dynamo.Deserialize1(Buf: buffer) -> (any, number)   Deserialize reads from the start of the buffer until the end and returns every top-level value.  Deserialize1 reads a single top-level value and returns (value, nextOffset).  local a, b = Dynamo.Deserialize(packet) local value, nextOffset = Dynamo.Deserialize1(one)

searchDocs.title: Deserialize with range / offset​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.DeserializeRange(Buf: buffer, Start: number, End: number?) -> ...any Dynamo.Deserialize1WOffset(Buf: buffer, Offset: number) -> (any, number)   DeserializeRange reads top-level values while Cursor < End (default end is buffer.len(Buf)).  Deserialize1WOffset starts at Offset and returns (value, nextOffset).

searchDocs.title: Push​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.Push(Buf: buffer, Offset: number, ...: any) -> number Dynamo.Push1(Buf: buffer, Offset: number, Value: any) -> number   Writes into an existing buffer starting at Offset and returns the cursor after the write. Useful for filling preallocated packets.  If a push errors mid-write, call Dynamo.Restore() so the internal scratch buffer is reset to the safe copy.

searchDocs.title: Scratch buffer size​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.SetWriteBufferSize(Size: number)   Replaces the internal write scratch buffer (default 1,000,000 bytes). Copy of existing content up to the previous size is preserved when possible.

searchDocs.title: Runtime constants​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.SetConstant(Constant: Constants, Value: any)   Tunes inference and wire layout. Name must be one of:  Constant	Type	Default	EffectSerInstanceSerialization	boolean	false	false → Instances use RefInstance; true → SerInstance (needs DefineSerInstanceSchema) InstanceRefMode	string	"Normal"	"Normal" → u16 ref id; "Extended" → u24 ref id UseQuaternion	boolean	true	true → QCframe (28b); false → matrix Cframe (48b) DoMapCompute	boolean	true	When true, map length picks Map8 / Map / Map24; when false, maps default to Map QuantizedScaleMin	number	0	Lower bound for UDim/UDim2 scale quantization QuantizedScaleMax	number	1	Upper bound for UDim/UDim2 scale quantization  Dynamo.SetConstant("UseQuaternion", false) Dynamo.SetConstant("SerInstanceSerialization", true) Dynamo.SetConstant("InstanceRefMode", "Extended")   Both ends of a session must use the same constants for buffers to round-trip correctly. Changing a constant does not rewrite already-encoded buffers.

searchDocs.title: Serializable instances​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.DefineSerInstanceSchema(ClassName: string, Schema: { [string]: number })   This is slightly contradicting the library purpose (schemaless), but while developing the library, I could not find a better way to efficiently serialize instances, the main purpose of this design is to stay performant and let users choose which properties to serialize.  Registers a property schema for value-style instance serialization (SerInstance). Schema values are type tag ids from Dynamo.Types (for example Dynamo.Types.Vec, Dynamo.Types.Color).  Enable with Dynamo.SetConstant("SerInstanceSerialization", true). Up to 255 schemas may be registered. Property payloads are untagged; the schema already names each property's type.  Instance references (RefInstance) do not use this API; they use the _VSID attribute maps maintained at module init (SerInstanceSerialization left false, the default).

searchDocs.title: Types table​
searchDocs.content: Dynamo.Types exposes numeric type tags (U8, Str8, Array, Vec, Cframe, QCframe, RefInstance, SerInstance, and the rest). This is only used for defining SerInstance schemas.

searchDocs.title: Dynamo throughput​
searchDocs.content: Source: benchresult/bench.txt Harness: bench/Bench.luau  Values are average microseconds per call (μs). Lower is faster.

searchDocs.title: Strings, buffers, and datatypes​
searchDocs.content: Type	RoundTrip (μs)String (10 chars)	0.12 String (100 chars)	0.16 Buf (32b)	0.15 Vector3	0.08 CFrame (quat)	0.16 Color3	0.10 UDim2	0.12 EnumItem	0.21

searchDocs.title: Collections​
searchDocs.content: Type	RoundTrip (μs)Array (1)	0.18 Array (10)	0.49 Array (100)	3.24 Map (1)	0.22 Map (10)	1.03 Map (100)	8.30  Primitive round trips sit around 0.08 μs. Cost grows mainly with collection size (per-element tags + payloads).

searchDocs.title: Versus VoidSentryUltimate and Sera​
searchDocs.content: This comparison is a bit unfair since VoidSentryUltimate and Sera do not infer types at runtime, but Dynamo still managed to keep up well.  Source: benchresult/compare.txt Harness: bench/Compare.luau Iterations: 10,000 per timed batch  Sera only serializes through schemas; the comparator wraps values in a single-field schema. VoidSentryUltimate uses typed nodes. Dynamo is schemaless (type tags on the wire).  RoundTrip wins in this run: VoidSentry 23, Dynamo 0, Sera 0 (of 23 cases).

searchDocs.title: Typical RoundTrip ratios (Dynamo ÷ VoidSentry)​
searchDocs.content: Case	Approx. ratioScalars / Bool / Vector3	~1.14× String8 / Buffer / Color3 / CFrame quat	~1.07–1.20× Array (10)	~1.6× Map (10)	~1.4× UDim2	~1.3× (Dynamo smaller on wire: 9b vs 16b)

searchDocs.title: Versus Sera​
searchDocs.content: On shared primitives and buffers, Dynamo is about 2× faster than Sera on RoundTrip (scalars ~0.08 μs vs ~0.16 μs). Sera stays slower on CFrame quat (~0.28 μs vs Dynamo 0.16 μs).

searchDocs.title: How to read this​
searchDocs.content: Schemaless tags cost ~1 byte and a small infer/dispatch cost versus schema-fixed VoidSentry nodes.Collection gaps are dominated by per-element tags (size and time).Prefer Dynamo when you want dynamic values without maintaining schemas; prefer a schema library when every field type is known and bandwidth/CPU are tighter.

searchDocs.title: Versus other dynamic serializers​
searchDocs.content: Source: benchresult/comparedynamic.txt Harness: bench/CompareDynamic.luau Iterations: 10,000 per timed batch  Compares Dynamo to BlazeSentry dynamic, BufferEncoder, MessagePack, and HttpService:JSONEncode / JSONDecode. Each library only runs on types it actually supports (Blaze has no nil / buffer / UDim2; MessagePack/JSON skip Roblox datatypes; BufferEncoder wraps non-tables and skips bare nil).  RoundTrip wins in this run: Dynamo 20, Blaze 0, BufferEncoder 0, MessagePack 0, JSON 0 (of 20).

searchDocs.title: Wire size (bytes)​
searchDocs.content: Case	Dynamo	Blaze	BE	MsgPack	JSONU8	2	2	5	1	2 Array (10)	22	22	22	11	22 Map (10)	63	64	63	42	73 CFrame	29	49	23	—	— UDim2	9	—	20	—	—

searchDocs.title: Takeaways​
searchDocs.content: Against other schemaless / dynamic encoders, Dynamo leads RoundTrip on every shared case in this run (~3.7× Blaze on scalars, ~6× BufferEncoder, ~5× JSON).MessagePack stays closest on small integers and dense numeric arrays (no per-element type tags). Dynamo still wins those cases here and leads on maps and Roblox datatypes MessagePack cannot encode.BufferEncoder pays for a table root + richer type system; size and time trail Dynamo on these fixtures.Blaze dynamic matches Dynamo’s wire size on many scalars but is ~3–4× slower RoundTrip here.Prefer Dynamo for mixed Roblox + Luau payloads without schemas; prefer MessagePack when the payload is MsgPack-only Luau data and array density matters.  Re-run locally:  require(path.to.Bench)(true) require(path.to.Compare)(true) require(path.to.CompareDynamic)(true)
